ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Hong Kong Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance (Cap. 615), Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) Part 15A on significant controllers registers, Limited Partnership Ordinance (Cap. 37), Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310), and, for the Chinese beneficial owner chain, the Measures for the Management of Beneficial Owner Information (PBOC/SAMR Order No. 3, effective 1 November 2024).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the Foreign-Invested Partnership / Limited Partnership
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Hong Kong Companies Registry (Registrar of Companies)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization before a Hong Kong notary public, followed by exactly one of two mutually exclusive paths: (i) Hague Apostille issued by the Hong Kong High Court for Apostille Convention member states; or (ii) Consular Legalization through the PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the consulate/embassy of the destination country for non-member states. Do not chain both sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certificate of Continuing Status / Certificate of Existence)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Hong Kong Companies Registry (Registrar of Companies) or licensed corporate services provider where permitted
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization of the issuing officer's signature, then either a Hague Apostille by the competent authority of the origin state (Hong Kong High Court for HK; PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs for Mainland China) or, for non-member states, Consular Legalization at the destination consulate. Apostille and consular legalization are parallel and mutually exclusive and must never be performed sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution / Power of Attorney authorizing the incorporation and instructing counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the non-resident corporate general partner (or all general partners if not a corporate partner)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Signatures notarized by a notary public, then apostilled by the country of origin if that country is an Apostille Convention member. If the country is not a member, have the notarized resolution authenticated by the issuing state's Ministry of Foreign Affairs and obtain Consular Legalization from the consulate of Hong Kong/China, as applicable. Never use both apostille and consular legalization in the same chain.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association / Limited Partnership Agreement (including UBO representation and PBOC/SAMR Order No. 3 acknowledgment)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Initial partners and Hong Kong-registered legal counsel, authenticated by notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization of all partner signatures/authorized signatories, then either a Hague Apostille certificate (for Apostille Convention member states) or a consular legalization certificate (for non-member states) on each original instrument. The two methods are alternatives; sequential chaining is prohibited.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter and good-standing credit check from the clearing bank maintaining the applicant's account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed bank in Hong Kong or applicant's home-country bank (e.g., HSBC, Standard Chartered, Bank of China Hong Kong)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank officer signature and corporate seal notarized, then if the bank's jurisdiction is an Apostille Convention member, apostille by the competent issuing authority; if non-member, place the original before the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and consulate of the receiving jurisdiction. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive; no layered chain of both.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All intended partners, general partners, limited partners, ultimate beneficial owners, directors, and authorized signatories must undergo enhanced due diligence against a consolidated screening universe composed of the OFAC SDN and Non-SDN lists, the UN Security Council consolidated list, Hong Kong financial sanctions lists maintained by the Commerce and Economic Development Bureau and the Hong Kong Monetary Authority, the EU consolidated list, and domestic PRC corruption and judicial disciplinary databases. Automated fuzzy matching must be followed by manual adjudication of phonetic, translation, and transliteration variants. Any positive match triggers enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth verification, senior-management approval, and ongoing transaction monitoring. PEPs are screened using a 12-month look-back, with annual re-screening and event-driven escalation. Self-declaration cannot substitute for independent database screening. This protocol applies before onboarding and continuously thereafter.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Partnership Ordinance (Cap. 38) and Limited Partnerships Ordinance (Cap. 37), sections 1-20; Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310), section 5, as applied in Hong Kong SAR
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies Registry, Limited Partnerships Registry, 14/F, Queensway Government Offices, Victoria, Hong Kong SAR; Business Registration Office, Inland Revenue Department
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of a Limited Partnership (Form LR1) and Statement of Particulars, together with the executed Limited Partnership Agreement
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. Hong Kong limited partnerships have no statutory minimum paid-up capital. The partners fix capital by agreement; the aggregate initial contribution of US$200,000 is booked on the capital ledger and held in ordinary partnership bank accounts. There is no blocked escrow account requirement.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTION OF THE GENERAL PARTNER AND THE MANAGEMENT COMMITTEE OF [PARTNERSHIP NAME] LIMITED PARTNERSHIP (THE 'PARTNERSHIP') IN LIEU OF A FIRST BOARD MEETING, ADOPTED ON [DATE], 2025.

WHEREAS:

A. The Partnership is being registered as a limited partnership under the Limited Partnerships Ordinance (Cap. 37) of Hong Kong and will carry on business as a vertical industrial enterprise resource planning and customer relationship software platform.

B. The partners have entered into a Limited Partnership Agreement dated [DATE] that vests management and control in the General Partner.

C. The General Partner and the Management Committee wish to formalize the initial capital, banking authorization, registered office, and statutory officer appointments.

D. The Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310) requires the Partnership to obtain and display a Business Registration Certificate.

NOW THEREFORE, IT IS RESOLVED AS FOLLOWS:

1. CAPITALIZATION AND SUBSCRIPTION. The initial capital subscription of the partners is hereby accepted and recorded. The General Partner subscribes for an unlimited interest in management and profits, and each Limited Partner subscribes for the fixed capital contribution set out in the capital account schedule. No share certificates are issued because the Partnership has no share capital. The aggregate initial paid-up capital is US$200,000, all in cash, to be deposited into the designated Partnership bank account within 30 days after registration. The bookkeeper shall maintain a separate capital ledger in accordance with section 7 of Cap. 37. No statutory minimum or blocked escrow requirement applies under Hong Kong law.

2. BANKING AUTHORIZATIONS. Any two signatures from the following persons are jointly and severally authorized to open banking facilities, execute credit mandates, accept financing covenants, and discharge negotiable instruments: [Name A, Management Committee Member]; [Name B, Management Committee Member]; and [Name C, General Partner Representative]. The depository bank is directed to accept this resolution together with a certificate of incumbency as complete authority. Stripe Billing and Direct Debit payment rails may be activated only after the corporate account is opened and AML verification is completed.

3. REGISTERED OFFICE. The registered office of the Partnership shall be at [Address, Hong Kong SAR]. The Companies Registry and the Business Registration Office shall be notified in writing of any change within fifteen days. The registered office is authorized to receive service of process for all statutory purposes.

4. STATUTORY APPOINTMENTS. The General Partner is appointed as the compliance principal. [Name] is appointed as Partnership Secretary with responsibility for annual returns and business registration renewal. [Firm] is appointed as auditor and tax agent. Each officer accepts office subject to the Limited Partnerships Ordinance and applicable anti-money laundering obligations.

5. GENERAL PROVISIONS. This resolution is binding on all partners and may be amended only by unanimous written consent. Certified copies shall be delivered to banks, the Business Registration Office, and the Companies Registry.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the General Partner has executed this resolution on the day and year first above written.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name availability search and preliminary de-risking
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry, Hong Kong SAR (ICRIS online search portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name availability search using the Integrated Companies Registry Information System (ICRIS). For a limited partnership, the proposed name must not be identical to an existing company or other restricted entity name. The English name must end with 'Limited Partnership' and the Chinese name may be in traditional characters. Record the search output in the dossier. If the desired name is unavailable, the general partner shall select a list of three alternative names and re-run the search. This protocol is a private pre-filing step but is a de facto requirement to prevent registry rejection and late fee exposure.
required_dossiers: Proposed entity name in English and Chinese
Identity of the intended general partner
Screenshot of reserved alternatives if any
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the chosen name is unavailable, select an alternative from the pre-cleared list, re-run the ICRIS search, and update the internal formation memorandum before proceeding.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Limited Partnership Agreement and Statement of Particulars
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public or licensed solicitor in Hong Kong for attestation of signatures
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the limited partnership agreement to govern profits, losses, capital calls, distributions, transfer restrictions, dissolution, and indemnification. Prepare the Statement of Particulars (Form LR1) containing the registered name, principal place of business, general partner details, limited partner details, capital contributions, and partnership term. Execute the agreement and Form LR1 before a notary public or an authorized witness. All partners must provide certified passport and proof of address so the notary can verify identity without further query. This step must be completed before any filing is submitted.
required_dossiers: Certified passport copy of each partner
Proof of residential or registered address of each partner
Certificate of incorporation or equivalent for corporate partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the solicitor or notary identifies inconsistencies in identity or contribution amounts, correct the discrepancy, re-execute the affected schedule, and obtain fresh notarial acknowledgment before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of registration application with the Companies Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry, Limited Partnerships Registry, Hong Kong SAR
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit Form LR1 together with the executed partnership agreement, the prescribed registration fee, and a covering letter from the registered solicitor. The Registrar will examine the particulars and may call for supporting declarations. Upon acceptance, the Registrar issues a Certificate of Registration of Limited Partnership and returns a certified copy of the filed particulars. The partners must immediately repair any discrepancy found in the certificate by filing a supplemental statement. No name change may occur before registration without a fresh application. All filing fees and any annual registration fee must be settled before issuance of the certificate.
required_dossiers: Proof of payment of registration fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a requisition or query, respond in writing within 14 days with an explanatory affidavit, clarification, and an amended Form LR1; pay any additional fee if the amendment changes the registered particulars.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Business Registration Office, Inland Revenue Department, Hong Kong SAR
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit Form IRBR200 to the Business Registration Office within one month of the commencement date. Attach a certified copy of the Certificate of Registration of Limited Partnership and proof of the registered office address. The office will issue a Business Registration Certificate, which must be displayed prominently at the registered office. The certificate is renewable annually upon payment of the prescribed business registration fee and levy. If the application is queried because the business description is too narrow, amend the description to include software publishing, cloud application hosting, and ERP/CRM services, and resubmit the form with a cover letter. Failure to register within the statutory window attracts penalties.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of Certificate of Registration of Limited Partnership
Identity document of the person executing the form
Application fee and levy payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Business Registration Office suspends or queries the application, correct the business description, pay any accrued late fee, and apply for re-issue; where the certificate is lost, apply for a certified replacement.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Banking onboarding and payment rail activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed bank operating under the Hong Kong Monetary Authority and relevant payment processor
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the certified Certificate of Registration of Limited Partnership, the Business Registration Certificate, and this formal resolution to a licensed Hong Kong bank. Complete the bank account opening forms, Know-Your-Customer questionnaire, FATCA/CRS self-certifications, and sign the banking mandate as authorized in Section 2 of the resolution. The bank will perform anti-money laundering and counter-financing of terrorism risk assessment; the entity is classified in the Low_Risk_Standard tier, so clearance is expected within ten working days. After the account is opened, activate Stripe Billing and Direct Debit rails by submitting merchant registration materials and executing the processor agreement.
required_dossiers: Certified Certificate of Registration of Limited Partnership
Source of funds and wealth declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional KYC information, provide the beneficial ownership chain, an undertaking letter, and audited capital source within three business days; if the application is declined, submit the same package to another licensed bank and notify the Business Registration Office of any change in registered office.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - the business is a pure digital software service under ISIC 6201 and has no physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing operations.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - vertical ERP/CRM cloud software does not require an industrial operating license in Hong Kong.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable - no Environmental Impact Assessment tier because there is no manufacturing or physical discharge activity.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - no wastewater, VOC, or hazardous waste generation; no quantitative thresholds apply.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable - there are no physical industrial premises requiring a Civil Defense fire permit, structural load inspection, or workplace safety approval beyond the landlord's commercial tenancy fire safety obligations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, including the Business Registration Office; online portal is the IRD eTAX system (www.ird.gov.hk). For the sovereign Mainland China component, the State Taxation Administration (STA) with its National Electronic Tax Bureau platform is the national authority, but Hong Kong is a separate tax jurisdiction for registration purposes.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) under the People's Bank of China (PBOC) for the onshore China Foreign-Invested Partnership, with the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) as the relevant authority for the Hong Kong SAR offshore treasury leg.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department - Business Registration Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually before the expiry date of the current Business Registration Certificate; a renewal notice is normally served by the Business Registration Office one month before the expiry date, and the applicable registration fee and levy must be settled by the expiry date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to renew renders the business certificate invalid. Penalty for operating without a valid business registration is a fine not exceeding HKD 5,000 (approximately USD 641), and for continuing default, a further daily fine; prosecution may also lead to imprisonment of up to six months.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Partnership Profits Tax Return - Form BIR52
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department, Profits Tax Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month from the date of issue of the tax return. Returns are generally issued on the first business day of April for financial periods ending the previous December; a concessionary extension of up to 30 June is available where a qualified tax representative is engaged for accounting periods ending 31 December.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties range from HKD 1,200 (approximately USD 154) to HKD 10,000 (approximately USD 1,282). If the Inland Revenue Department considers the failure to be wilful or without reasonable excuse, it may claim additional tax of up to three times the amount of tax undercharged and may issue an estimated assessment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employer's Return of Remuneration and Pensions - Form BIR56A and BIR56B (if staff are employed)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department, Employer Returns Unit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month from the date of issue of the employer's return, normally issued in April each year. A short automatic extension is allowed for returns submitted electronically through eTAX, as specified in the issuing notice.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A penalty of up to HKD 10,000 (approximately USD 1,282) may be imposed for late filing or failure to file; for deliberate evasion, a further assessment of up to three times the amount of tax that would have been undercharged may be issued, and the employer may be prosecuted.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registration of Changes in Partnership Particulars
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 days after any change in the general or limited partners, partner capital contributions, profit-sharing ratios, nature of business, or registered office of a limited partnership registered under the Limited Partnerships Ordinance (Cap 37).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance with the filing obligation means the changing partner(s) may remain liable for partnership debts incurred after the change, and the partnership may be refused service; monetary penalties may also apply under prescribed provisions for failure to deliver the required notice.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: For a Hong Kong registered partnership, there is no automatic statutory audit imposed solely by the partnership form. However, an independent certified public accountant audit is legally mandatory when any one of the following quantitative thresholds or conditions is reached: (1) annual gross receipts or gross turnover exceeds HKD 1,000,000 (approximately USD 128,200), in which case the Inland Revenue Department requires audited financial statements to accompany the Form BIR52 Profits Tax Return; (2) the partnership is registered as a Limited Partnership Fund or carries on a financially regulated activity under the Securities and Futures Ordinance, where audited financial statements are unconditionally required regardless of turnover; (3) the Inland Revenue Department issues a specific notice under section 51C of the Inland Revenue Ordinance calling for audited accounts; (4) the partnership is a parent or subsidiary within a Hong Kong corporate group that is required to present consolidated audited accounts under the Companies Ordinance; or (5) a banking lender, investor, or financing agreement imposes an audit covenant irrespective of statutory requirements. No headcount-based audit trigger exists for partnerships under Hong Kong law, but once employees are engaged, separate employer tax reporting obligations arise.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Hong Kong Financial Reporting Standards (HKFRS), which are fully converged with International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS). A partnership not required to produce consolidated accounts may instead apply the HKFRS for Private Entities framework, a simplified self-contained set of standards, or a basis of accounting accepted by the Inland Revenue Department provided that the records clearly support the assessable profits computation.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Hong Kong maintains no public UBO register for ordinary partnerships and limited partnerships. However, the partnership's licensed Trust or Company Service Provider (TCSP) is obliged to conduct customer due diligence and to refresh beneficial ownership identification at least once every 12 months, or immediately upon any occasion of money laundering suspicion. Changes in the composition of general or limited partners and any change in control or profit-sharing percentages must be recorded internally, and a formal statutory notice of the change must be delivered to the Companies Registry within 7 days under the Limited Partnerships Ordinance. In addition, an annual partner confirmation protocol applies: each partner holding an economic interest of 25% or more must confirm his or her UBO profile in writing within 30 days of a transfer of interest, and the registered agent must preserve the updated ownership map in the statutory books. Failure to maintain or refresh this information can attract AML penalties of up to HKD 100,000 (approximately USD 12,820) per offence, with possible conviction for responsible officers.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Limited and General Partners with Capital Contributions and Profit-Sharing Entitlements
Register of Charges, Pledges and Mortgages over Partnership Assets
Partnership Meetings and Resolutions Minute Book
Beneficial Ownership and Significant Controllers Register maintained for AML/CTF compliance

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 800 - 2,200 per annum for a Hong Kong registered office address, registered agent and routine partnership secretarial administration
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 - 6,000 per annual audit engagement, depending on transaction volume, turnover level and accounting complexity

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 16.5% standard corporate Profits Tax rate (8.25% concessionary rate on first HKD 2,000,000 assessable profit for corporations; for the FIP, as an unincorporated pass-through entity, the two-tier rates of 7.5% on first HKD 2,000,000 and 15% above apply at partner level)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Hong Kong offers territorial source relief so foreign-sourced income is exempt; no capital gains tax; no VAT/GST; 100% HK-based profits trigger Profits Tax. Enhanced tax deduction of up to 300% for qualifying R&D expenditure (first HKD 2,000,000), 200% for remainder; free-zone incentives not applicable in HK; FIP pass-through is not taxed at entity level.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: BIR52 - Profits Tax Return for Partnerships (Hong Kong Inland Revenue Department) filed via eTAX/Integrated Tax System
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (year of assessment basis; BIR52 is issued for each profits-tax year)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 1 month from the date of issue of the return by the IRD; for financial periods ended in December, the IRD normally grants an extension to 15 August when e-Filing is adopted

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partnership name and Hong Kong Business Registration number
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the exact name on the Business Registration Certificate and include the branch BR number. Non-resident partners should ensure a service address in Hong Kong is stated.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Principal place of business in Hong Kong and place of central management
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State physical office, registered address and where key board decisions are made. For tax residence and treaty access, ensure the Core Income-Generating Activities of the ERP/CRM cloud business are not merely paper-based in HK.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Nature of business and principal activities
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use ISIC 6201 / NAICS 511210 - Vertical Industrial ERP and CRM software publishing. Describe the subscription, SaaS hosting, recurring implementation and support revenue; identify the foreign invested partners.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Basis period and year of assessment
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State first and last day of the accounting period. For a 31 December year-end, YA 2024/25 basis period is 1 January 2024 to 31 December 2024 unless changed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profit or loss per financial statements as adjusted
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter accounting profit from HK books before tax adjustments. Reconcile to IFRS; any Partner current account drawings are not deducted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Additions: non-deductible expenses, disallowable items, and provisions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back general reserves, political donations, self-serving expenses, depreciation if not claimed, and any penalty fines. Cross-border allocation of group management charges must be arm's-length and supported by CUP or TNMM documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions: non-taxable income, capital gains, offshore profits justified by claim
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For FIP, deduct capital gains and genuinely foreign-sourced income after satisfying the offshore claim test. The IRD scrutinizes software cloud revenue: server location, customers, brokers and operations determine source.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Assessable profits (adjusted profits) after applying loss relief
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute the correction: net profit plus non-deductible expenses minus exempt offshore income minus loss relief. Hong Kong statutory law allows indefinite loss carry-forward, but within the constraints of this whitepaper the line reports using a 5-year carry-forward scheduling ceiling.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partnership allocation of assessable profits to individual partners
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate according to the partnership deed. For non-resident partners, the share of HK-source profits is assessable under section 15(1)(b) and must be declared with individual Profits Tax returns; do not declare partnership-level dividends.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of non-resident partner particulars and elective two-tier tax calculation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: List non-resident partner's name, percentage of profits, Tax Residency Certificate and address. The two-tier rates apply on the partner's allocable share where the partner is an individual; corporate partners are taxed at 16.5%.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: maximum fine of HKD 10,000 and potential additional tax up to 10% of undercharged tax for negligent non-compliance; for fraud, fine up to HKD 50,000 and three times the tax undercharged, plus imprisonment up to 3 years on indictment. IRD may also make estimated assessments with no loss relief if returns are overdue.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% - Hong Kong imposes no dividend withholding tax on distribution of profits by an FIP to any partner (resident or non-resident); no DTA is needed to receive a HK dividend free of WHT.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Although no WHT arises, a non-resident partner seeking treaty benefits in connection with offshore income or royalties must: (1) obtain a Hong Kong Tax Residency Certificate from the IRD; (2) provide a valid certificate from the treaty partner; (3) confirm beneficial ownership of the relevant income or interest; (4) file an advance ruling or notification with the IRD if invoking the Hong Kong-Mainland Arrangement; and (5) retain capacity, substance and accounting records. For royalties paid from Hong Kong to a Mainland China resident, the effective domestic tax of 4.95% is below the 7% treaty ceiling, so no additional treaty relief is required; to claim an exemption or reduced rate under another DTA, the payer must obtain IRD confirmation before paying the non-resident gross amount without deduction.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory: Royalties paid to non-resident corporate recipients are deemed to be 30% of the gross royalty and then taxed at 16.5%, producing an effective withholding-equivalent tax of 4.95% (4.5% for non-corporate recipients). Interest paid by the FIP to non-residents is generally not subject to HK WHT unless the lender carries on business in Hong Kong and the interest is sourced there, in which case profits tax of 16.5% may apply; treaty rates for interest are typically 7% under the Hong Kong-Mainland arrangement.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File required where annual turnover exceeds HKD 100 million and specified intercompany transactions exceed HKD 10 million; Master File required where group consolidated turnover exceeds HKD 600 million. For FIPs below these thresholds, contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation is still strongly recommended for the vertical CRM/ERP cross-border services.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Hong Kong has not enacted Caribbean-style Economic Substance Regulations (ESR). However, the IRD applies a real economic substance test in determining the source of profits: the FIP must demonstrate Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) in Hong Kong if it claims Hong Kong tax residence, including local office, employees, decision-making, IP ownership and cloud hosting. A shell FIP benefiting from treaty provisions without substance will be attacked under sections 61A or 61 of the Inland Revenue Ordinance and may be denied treaty benefits by the other contracting state.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Fraudulent False Tax Returns
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Adviser or director knowingly includes in the FIP's BIR52 a false statement of assessable profits, e.g., omitting recurring cloud subscription revenue sourced in Hong Kong or falsely claiming that CRM implementation fees are offshore income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Inland Revenue Ordinance s.82(1): on indictment, a fine of up to HKD 50,000 plus three times the tax undercharged and imprisonment up to 3 years; on summary conviction, a fine up to HKD 10,000 and imprisonment up to 6 months.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced for knowingly concerned directors and general partners: they face civil restitution of tax and interest, a departure prevention order or travel ban from Hong Kong, seizure of personal assets, disqualification as company director, and criminal imprisonment up to 3 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file BIR52 within the statutory period without reasonable excuse after receiving IRD demand, or intentionally suppressing partnership returns to allow IRD to make estimated assessments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: s.80(2) IRO: fine up to HKD 10,000; the IRD may raise estimated assessment and recover interest plus a further penalty up to 10% of the tax undercharged; non-compliance also triggers a failure to comply notice under s.80(1).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: If the general partner or director is the one responsible for filing, the court can order personal payment of the FIP's outstanding tax debts under piercing principles; a mandatory departure prevention order may be imposed under the Inland Revenue Ordinance to stop the director from leaving Hong Kong while tax is unpaid; repeated offences carry imprisonment up to 6 months.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Sham Transfer Pricing Arrangement
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the FIP as a paper vehicle with no physical presence, no substantive employees in Hong Kong, intercompany payments for ERP/CRM license royalties or cloud services without an arm's-length fee, and using tax residency or DTA benefits to move profits out of Hong Kong while transferring economic functions to a Mainland affiliate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Section 61A IRO anti-avoidance: assessments adjusted as if the transaction had not been entered into; penalties up to 100% of the undercharged tax; transfer pricing adjustments under s.50AB; in egregious criminal cases, common law conspiracy to defraud or money laundering prosecutions (e.g., Drugs Trafficking and Organized Crime Ordinance) with fines up to HKD 1,000,000 and imprisonment up to 14 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts will pierce the veil to hold directors/general partners personally liable for restitution of extracted profits, monetary penalties and legal costs; the IRD may apply for a Mareva injunction freezing personal assets and a travel ban; imprisonment can reach 7 years where the shell vehicle is used as part of a tax fraud conspiracy and 14 years where money laundering charges are proven.
